verses.1: Am I not free? Am I not a messenger? Have I not seen Jesus, our Lord? Are you not in charge of my work?
verses.2: If I am not an apostle to others, then surely I am one to you. For you are the seal of my mission among you.
verses.3: This is my apology to those who are examining me.
verses.4: Don’t we have the right to eat and drink?
verses.5: We certainly do not have the authority to take a wife along with us, just like the other apostles, and also the brothers of the Lord and Caiaphas.
verses.6: Or do we not both, I and Barnabas, have the right not to act?
verses.7: Whoever plants seeds for their own enjoyment never eats them. Whoever grows vines and doesn’t eat its fruits? Whoever makes cheese and doesn’t eat it from that cheese?
verses.8: I’m not speaking in a human manner here. And isn’t that also what the law says as well?
verses.9: For in Moses’ law it is written: “Do not slaughter cattle during their menstrual periods.” Do not associate with those who are menstruating.
verses.10: Or does he say this completely on our behalf? For it was written on our behalf that the poor are to be treated with kindness, and the rich should expect to receive kindness in return.
verses.11: If we have given you our spiritual things, then have we not also greatly cared for your physical needs?
verses.12: If others also have part in your authority, aren’t we even more fortunate? But we do not use this authority for our own benefit. Instead, we give it all to the sake of not allowing anyone to stand in the way of the gospel of Christ.
verses.13: Didn’t you know that those who perform religious rituals eat the food from the temple? They also participate in the sacrifices that take place at the altar.
verses.14: And so, the Lord commanded those who are to spread the gospel to live according to its teachings.
verses.15: I, however, do not desire anything of this kind. I did not write these things in order for them to happen to me. It would be better for me to die then… After all, no one will be able to take my honor away from me.
verses.16: For if I preach the good news, it isn’t a source of pride for me; rather, it’s a necessity for me. It’s not a pleasure for me to preach the good news. It’s not a pleasure at all unless I do so.
verses.17: For if I do this alone, I will have a salary. But if I do it together with others, then I can surely manage my finances.
verses.18: So, what is my reward? It is to serve the gospel wholeheartedly, without using my authority over it in any way.
verses.19: For I am free from all obligations; therefore, I have become my own slave, so that I may win over those who are more important to me.
verses.20: And I became a Jew, just like the Jews. This was to win over the Jews. To those who were under the law, I also became under the law, not being myself under the law, so that I could win over those who were under the law.
verses.21: To those who are wicked, as if they were also wicked. But I am not wicked in the eyes of God; I am only “wicked” in the eyes of Christ, so that I can win over those who are wicked.
verses.22: I became weak for those who were weak, so that I could win them over. I became everything for all people, so that I could save some of them.
verses.23: But I always do this out of love for the gospel, so that I can become united with it.
verses.24: Don’t you know that those who run in the race actually run, but only one person will receive the prize? That’s why you need to run properly in order to win.
verses.25: But every one who competes deserves to receive a reward. Those people, then, will receive a faded crown; we, on the other hand, will receive something that never fades.
verses.26: I therefore move in such a way that it isn’t actually real; I move with such speed that it doesn’t really happen.
verses.27: But I cover my body with a veil and become a slave to it. So that no one else can claim that it’s not genuine.
